fact: The Sudan Times describes Bankak as one of Sudan's most widely used banking applications, used by customers to pay traders in Darfur.
Zakher, a Sudanese digital wallet, offers payments, transfers and daily services and launched a recurring debit order API on 24 August 2026, per Zakhir Wallet.
Al Jazeera reports that bank mobile applications are now widely used in Sudanese markets for transfers between individuals and traders, driven by the cash shortage.
Sudan Horizon says the Bede wallet, a Zain fintech service, was launched in April 2025 and offers app, USSD and web access with agents and merchants.
Sudan Horizon says the BBAN service lets Bede wallet users send and receive funds across all Sudanese banks.

Al Arabiya reports that millions of Sudanese use Bank of Khartoum's Bankak app for everyday transfers and payments (transport, fuel, treatment, food, government payments), and that it suffered disruptions in early October 2026.

Banking expert Abdullatif Ali Ibrahim says Bankak, the Bank of Khartoum app, remains Sudan's leading digital transfer platform, used for daily and commercial transactions, with Fawry and other bank services also operating (Dabanga).
The Sudan Times describes Bankak, run by Bank of Khartoum, as Sudan's dominant mobile payment application, used by businesses for electronic payments until its outage on 2 September 2026.
CBOS Circular 7/2026 permits banks, licensed mobile-payment institutions and payment providers to open e-wallets, transfer money, pay bills and take merchant payments over USSD.
